references.text: The same warning against making a covenant with the people of the land and their gods, for fear that it will become a snare to Israel.
The command not to make a covenant with the peoples in the land and the warning that they will lead Israel into idolatry.
Joshua's warning against marrying and making covenants with the remaining peoples, which will become a snare to Israel.
The angel of the Lord rebukes Israel for making covenants with the people of the land, in violation of God's command.
Israel was invited to idol sacrifices and ate from the sacrificial meals, just as warned in this verse.
Solomon's foreign wives turned his heart to other gods, fulfilling the warning in this verse.
Israel clung to Baal-Peor and ate offerings to dead gods, as described in the warning.
Paul warns against having fellowship with demons through idol sacrifices, parallel to the warning about eating from pagan altars.
Hosea describes Israel's spiritual adultery by offering on the high places and burning incense to other gods.
Ezekiel uses the concept of adultery to describe Israel's unfaithfulness in turning to idols.
Complementary warnings that the inhabitants will become a 'snare' through religious mixing.
A direct parallel in legislation linking covenant-making with the danger of idolatry.
Complementary warnings: Exodus points to religious temptation, while Numbers highlights the practical threat to the people.
Prophecy about the fulfillment of the fear expressed in Exodus: that prosperity will lead to turning to other gods.
Historical reference to breaking the specific command not to make a covenant with the inhabitants.
Theological connection between the warning against eating sacrifices (Exodus) and the judgment on those who break the covenant (Joshua).
Theological parallel: Both use 'fornication' as a metaphor for religious unfaithfulness to Yahweh.
Concrete application of the warning: How to avoid the 'snare' described in Exodus.
Repetition of the prophecy that the people will commit 'fornication with foreign gods,' just as warned in Exodus.
